title: Model Supply Heuristics: Rapid Prioritization for Fallback-Ready Inventory
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Build a lightweight heuristic and scoring pipeline to prioritize candidate open-source and third-party model variants for inclusion in Redwood's 'fallback-ready' inventory. The goal is to produce a ranked list (top 25) of models per serving use-case (chat-generation, embeddings, short-context RAG) that balance availability, cost delta, latency envelope, and integration effort so that runtime and product teams can configure automated fallback policies with confidence.

Background: Recent spikes in provider throttles and supply outages exposed gaps between 'models we can theoretically serve' and 'models we can safely fallback to without manual intervention.' Existing model scouting outputs are rich on capability and accuracy but lack a concise, action-oriented readiness score that correlates with ops effort to onboard, expected token-cost delta, and regional availability.

Scope:
- Define heuristic dimensions and measurement signals (availability, license/TOU risk, quantization compatibility, hardware affinity, latency tail, regressions on core prompt suite, provenance maturity).
- Implement a scoring prototype combining metric normalization and simple rules for hard rejects (e.g., incompatible license, inability to quantize under target memory).
- Produce a ranked export for three product verticals: API-hosted chat, Dedicated low-latency endpoints, and Embeddings for vector search.
- Deliver a short runbook for runtime engineers describing expected integration steps and rollback criteria for each ranked model.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- We prioritize speed over perfect statistical models for v1: heuristic must be computable with signals we can gather in 7 days.
- Coverage across regions will be probabilistic; where feature signals are absent we add an explicit penalty to the score.
- Some high-quality models may be deprioritized because of license friction or quantization risk — acceptable for fallback inventory where predictability matters more than marginal quality gains.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Heuristic spec doc reviewed and approved by Runtime and Research (owners: @Liam and @Priya).
2) Automated job produces ranked CSV for 3 verticals covering at least 25 models each.
3) Pilot rollout configured in staging: one can flip a canary fallback route to use top-3 fallback models and observe behavior for 48h without manual intervention.
4) Playbook and onboarding checklist published in Confluence.

Deliverables:
- Heuristic spec (Confluence) and scoring script (Python) in a short-lived repo.
- Ranked artifact CSV + explanation column per model (why scored high/low).
- Runbook and integration checklist.
- Post-mortem template for failed fallbacks.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in manual fallback runs during outages by 60% in the pilot.
- Mean time to enable a fallback model reduced from 2 person-days to <4 hours for new model candidates.
- Fallback cost delta (tokens*price) within target band for 80% of use-cases in pilot.

Stakeholders:

- Runtime/Engineering: Priya Gupta (serving runtime), Marco Alvarez (ops)
- Research: Dr. Ethan Park (eval suite)
- Solutions/Support: Helena Ortiz

Notes on deliverable ownership: Scoring script + CSV generation will live in a small repo (owned by Liam). Runbook and playbook will be Confluence-first (PM writes, Runtime reviews). Final artifacts to be linked into Redwood Console as a one-off dataset for operations to consume.
